patches.new_disclaimer: The Mississippi's main stem forms all or part of the border of, or flows through, exactly 10 states. Ordered north to south. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

The Continental Divide separates Pacific-draining watersheds from Atlantic/Gulf-draining watersheds. In the US, it runs through five contiguous states plus Alaska. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
The AT passes through 14 states between Springer Mountain (GA) and Mount Katahdin (ME). Ordered south to north. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
The PCT crosses only three states between the Mexican and Canadian borders. Ordered south to north. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Counts centerline miles of designated Interstate routes only (not other freeways). Ordered longest to shortest. Includes Washington DC.
Counts public-use airports (public and private-owned but open to the public) as tallied by the FAA. Includes Washington DC.
Counts entries in the National Bridge Inventory (spans of at least 20 feet on public roads). Includes both state-owned and locally-owned bridges. Includes Washington DC.
Counts of GNIS features with feature class 'Summit' by state. Every named summit is counted regardless of elevation. Includes Washington DC.
Named summits above 5,000 ft (1,524 m) with recognized names in Peakbagger's state databases. Elevation cutoff is fixed, not prominence-adjusted. DC not included (source omits it).
Total land area of federally recognized American Indian reservations plus off-reservation trust lands within each state's boundaries. DC not included (source omits it).
Sum of maximum normal storage across all dams in each state as recorded in the National Inventory of Dams. Interstate reservoirs are credited to the state hosting the dam. Includes Washington DC.
Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Falls' by state. Includes all named cascades regardless of drop height. DC not included (source omits it).
Non-federal plus federal rangeland acres as classified by NRCS. Rangeland is distinct from cropland and pastureland. DC not included (source omits it).
Timberland and other forestland classified by FIA as softwood forest-type groups (pine, fir, spruce, hemlock, cedar, redwood). Alaska's boreal forests are included. DC not included (source omits it).

Total land area of all islands lying within a state's legal boundaries, including inhabited and uninhabited islands in oceans, gulfs, sounds, lakes, and rivers. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Named barrier islands as inventoried by USGS coastal geology surveys. Excludes barrier spits still attached to the mainland. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Canyon' by state. Reflects naming convention as much as underlying topography. DC not included (source omits it).
Longest single named river whose entire course lies within one state's boundaries. Rivers that cross state lines are excluded. Includes Washington DC.
Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Plateau' or 'Mesa' by state. Reflects Southwestern mesa-country naming density. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Bay' by state, including tidal, lake, and river bays. Includes Washington DC.
